answer: **Hypothesis (data-grounded):** In the domain of **Economics**, the majority of authors tend to be male for both the original and the replication studies. Using the raw replication-projects dataset (141 unique original/replication pairs; ml1/ml3 collapsed to their aggregated rows, ee/rpp single rows), Economics is the only discipline where a strict majority of O/R pairs are majority-male on BOTH sides: 10 of 18 pairs (55.6%), versus Cognitive 18/49 (36.7%) and Social 20/74 (27.0%) — all clearly above their own within-discipline base rates too (Economics also leads marginally: original-side majority-male 14/18 = 77.8%, replication-side 13/18 = 72.2%). This holds under the primary strict rule (ratio > 0.5) and the "at least half" sensitivity rule (Economics 15/18 = 83.3% vs Cognitive 61.2%, Social 56.8%), so there is no rule disagreement to flag. **Caveat:** Economics is covered only by the 18-pair Experimental Economics (ee) replication project, a small sample, so the conclusion is directionally strong but rests on limited N; Economics is nonetheless the clear standout versus the all-discipline both-sides base rate of 48/141 = 34.0%.

payload.hypothesis: In the domain of Economics, the majority of authors tend to be male for both original and replication studies: 10 of 18 Economics O/R pairs (55.6%) are majority-male on both sides (authors_male.o > 0.5 AND authors_male.r > 0.5), versus 36.7% in Cognitive (18/49) and 27.0% in Social (20/74), and an all-discipline base rate of 34.0% (48/141). Economics also has the highest single-side majorities (original 77.8%, replication 72.2%). The result is robust to the tie rule: under the 'at least half' (>=0.5) variant Economics still leads (83.3% vs 61.2% Cognitive, 56.8% Social). Caveat: the Economics estimate rests on only 18 pairs, all from the Experimental Economics (ee) replication project, so it is a small-N finding, though it clearly stands out from the overall base rate.
payload.workflow: Loaded the raw study dataset (927 rows x 57 cols). Deduplicated to 141 unique O/R pairs (id): kept aggregated=True rows for ml1/ml3 (26 pooled replication-team rows) and the single rows for ee/rpp (115). Computed majority-male flags for both rules (>0.5 strict, >=0.5 sensitivity) on authors_male.o and authors_male.r, formed the conjunction flag, and tabulated counts/shares per discipline plus the all-discipline base rate. Diagnostics: 0.5 ties (33 o-side, 27 r-side pairs), drop=True pair handling (robustness, n=131, winner unchanged), and pair-level output table saved. The Fisher-z replication-success file was inspected and excluded (no author-gender columns).
